To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
hyperosmolar stress activates the Na(+)–H(+) exchanger and increases intracellular pH (i.e., intracellular alkalosis).
exposure of cardiac muscle to hyperosmotic solutions results in an alkalosis that is caused by the activation of the sodium‐hydrogen exchanger.
exposure of cardiac cells to hyperosmotic solutions results in activation of the Na(+)-H(+) antiporter, which causes intracellular alkalinisation.

the role of Na(+) in excitation‐contrac tion coupling in cardiac muscle.
the role of intracellular pH (i.e., the pH of the cytosol) in cardiac muscle.
the effects of hyperosmolar (hypertonic) solutions on cardiac function.
